The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function. A complex Hilbert space is a complete complex inner-product space, with inner product linear in its first variable. A self-adjoint operator $T$ is densely defined and satisfies $D(T)=D(T^*)$ and $T\psi=T^*\psi$ on that domain; nonnegative means $\langle T\psi,\psi\rangle\ge0$ for every $\psi\in D(T)$. A grading operator $\Gamma$ is a bounded self-adjoint involution, so its $+1$ and $-1$ eigenspaces are orthogonal; an operator $T$ is odd when $D(T)$ is $\Gamma$-invariant and $T\Gamma=-\Gamma T$ there. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. A **pure-point physical index datum** consists of a specified physical model record and its operator data. The model record identifies the spacetime and spatial domain, metric and orientation, global gauge group including its global form, field bundles and representations, adopted action or other postulates, and boundary conditions; it also states whether the Hilbert-space operators are constructed directly or obtained from a named regulator and measure. These are supplied model inputs, not conclusions of this definition. When curved spacetime is used, the record includes fixed Riemannian spin geometry, spin and R-symmetry data, and the model-specific spinor equation as in the earlier background definition; no claim is made that arbitrary geometry admits such data. The operator data include a complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H=\mathcal H^+\oplus\mathcal H^-$ as an orthogonal sum of closed subspaces, and the grading operator $\Gamma$ equal to $+I$ on $\mathcal H^+$ and $-I$ on $\mathcal H^-$. They supply a closed densely defined self-adjoint operator $\mathcal Q$ with domain invariant under $\Gamma$ and $\mathcal Q\Gamma\psi=-\Gamma\mathcal Q\psi$ on that domain. Set $K=\mathcal Q^2$ on $D(K)=\{\psi\in D(\mathcal Q):\mathcal Q\psi\in D(\mathcal Q)\}$ and require that $K$ is nonnegative and self-adjoint. The grading is dimensionless; if $K$ has energy units, $\mathcal Q$ has energy dimension $1/2$.

Require an orthogonal pure-point decomposition

$$\mathcal H=\mathcal H_0^+\oplus\mathcal H_0^-\oplus\widehat{\bigoplus}_{\lambda\in\Sigma}(\mathcal H_\lambda^+\oplus\mathcal H_\lambda^-),$$

where $\Sigma\subset(0,\infty)$ is a supplied countable set of distinct eigenvalues, $\mathcal H_0^\pm=\ker K\cap\mathcal H^\pm$ are finite-dimensional, and each $\mathcal H_\lambda^\pm=\ker(K-\lambda I)\cap\mathcal H^\pm$ is finite-dimensional and contained in $D(K)$. A compatible complete orthonormal basis $E=E^+\sqcup E^-$ of these subspaces is supplied as part of the data. For each $\beta>0$, also supply a bounded diagonal operator $T_\beta$ with eigenvalue $1$ on $E\cap\ker K$ and $e^{-\beta\lambda}$ on $E\cap(\mathcal H_\lambda^+\oplus\mathcal H_\lambda^-)$, and require $T_\beta$ to be trace class. The parameter $\beta$ has units of inverse energy when $K$ has energy units; in dimensionless radial-quantization conventions it is dimensionless.

The **Witten index** of this datum is the absolutely convergent graded heat supertrace, defined by the supplied basis rather than by an unproved basis-independence claim,

$$W_E(\beta)=\sum_{e\in E^+}\langle T_\beta e,e\rangle-\sum_{e\in E^-}\langle T_\beta e,e\rangle,\qquad \beta>0,$$

where each heat operator is trace class, meaning compact with summable singular values, and the supplied-basis diagonal sums are absolutely convergent; the sums are taken over finite subsets and then their absolutely convergent limits. This signed supertrace is not a raw state degeneracy. The zero-gap subspace singled out by the selected supercharge is $\ker K=\mathcal H_0^+\oplus\mathcal H_0^-$. Equality of the full heat supertrace with the even-minus-odd dimension of this subspace is a separate conditional theorem under the exact hypotheses. A physical model may call this a **BPS index** only when its own supercharge algebra identifies this kernel with a specified BPS-saturated sector. Here a BPS-saturated state means a nonzero domain vector in a specified massive rest fiber satisfying the mass/central-charge equality in the earlier BPS definition. The present definition does not identify every BPS state with $\ker K$ and asserts no such state exists.

For every pure-point graded trace-class index datum with positive-energy blocks paired by the unitary maps $U_\lambda=Q/\sqrt\lambda$ proved from its supercharge data, the absolutely convergent supertrace satisfies

$$W(\beta)=m_0^+-m_0^-\qquad\text{for every }\beta>0.$$

Thus it is independent of $\beta$ and equals the even-minus-odd dimension of the zero-energy subspace. This is a conditional mathematical statement for the discrete trace-class data in the definition; it asserts no continuum cancellation, regularized trace identity, or physical index formula.

The physical model record remains an adopted input; no property of its continuum construction is inferred.
Apply [F2] to this identical operator datum. It gives $W_E(\beta)=m_0^+-m_0^-=\dim\mathcal H_0^+-\dim\mathcal H_0^-$ for every $\beta>0$, which is independent of $\beta$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. A complex Hilbert space is a complete complex inner-product space, with inner product linear in its first variable. A self-adjoint operator $T$ is densely defined and satisfies $D(T)=D(T^*)$ and $T\psi=T^*\psi$ there; nonnegative means $\langle T\psi,\psi\rangle\ge0$ for all $\psi\in D(T)$. A grading operator $\Gamma$ is a bounded self-adjoint involution; its $+1$ and $-1$ eigenspaces are orthogonal, and a densely defined operator $T$ is odd if $D(T)$ is $\Gamma$-invariant and $T\Gamma=-\Gamma T$ there. For operators $A,B$, $D(AB)=\{\psi\in D(B):B\psi\in D(A)\}$ is the composition domain. A Hilbert basis is a complete orthonormal family. Let $S^3=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:|x|=1\}$ have its round metric and standard orientation. The **radial Hilbert space** $\mathcal H_{S^3}$ is the complex Hilbert space supplied by the chosen physical model after quantization on this unit spatial three-sphere; its construction is model input, not proved here. The model record names its gauge group and global form, matter representations, action or other adopted postulates, and the Hilbert-space construction or regulator and measure; the spatial sphere has no boundary, and any other boundary or domain conditions are stated as input. The rotation group is $\operatorname{Spin}(4)=SU(2)_1\times SU(2)_2$. Let $E$ be the dimensionless self-adjoint conformal Hamiltonian, $J_1,J_2$ the self-adjoint Cartan generators of the two rotation factors, and $R$ the self-adjoint $U(1)_R$ charge. Normalize $R$ so that the chosen right-handed Poincare supercharge $Q=\widetilde Q_{\dot -}$ has $R$-charge $+1$ and $J_2$-weight $-\tfrac12$; it has $J_1$-weight zero. Its actual Hilbert adjoint in radial quantization is the conformal supercharge $Q^\dagger=\widetilde S^{\dot -}$. The model supplies a closed densely defined operator $Q$ and its actual Hilbert adjoint $Q^\dagger$, a grading operator $\Gamma$, and a dense linear domain $\mathcal D$ invariant under $\Gamma,Q,Q^\dagger$ and contained in $D(Q^2)\cap D((Q^\dagger)^2)\cap D(QQ^\dagger)\cap D(Q^\dagger Q)$. Require $Q,Q^\dagger$ to be odd, $Q^2=(Q^\dagger)^2=0$ on $\mathcal D$, and the exact positive self-adjoint operator relation

$$\Delta=\frac12\{Q,Q^\dagger\}=E-2J_2-\frac32R\ge0.$$

The protected sector is $\ker\Delta=\ker Q\cap\ker Q^\dagger$, since on the common domain $\langle\Delta\psi,\psi\rangle=\tfrac12(\|Q\psi\|^2+\|Q^\dagger\psi\|^2)$. Define the two dimensionless commuting charges

$$J_+=J_1+J_2+\frac12R,\qquad J_-=J_2-J_1+\frac12R.$$

On a separately supplied dense domain $D(\mathsf Q)\subseteq D(Q)\cap D(Q^\dagger)$, define the odd operator $\mathsf Q=(Q+Q^\dagger)/\sqrt2$ and require it to be self-adjoint and to satisfy $\mathsf Q^2=\Delta$ as a closed-operator equality. Its domain is $\Gamma$-invariant and $\Gamma\mathsf Q=-\mathsf Q\Gamma$ there. Supply a simultaneous pure-point decomposition for $\Delta,J_+,J_-$ and $\Gamma$, with a compatible complete orthonormal basis $\mathcal B=\mathcal B^+\sqcup\mathcal B^-$. More explicitly, the basis vectors have real charge eigenvalues $(\lambda,a,b)$, with $\lambda\ge0$, and span the joint subspaces $\mathcal H_{\lambda,a,b}^\pm$; the distinct joint labels form a supplied countable set. Each closed self-adjoint charge has its maximal diagonal domain: for eigenvalues $d_e$ its domain consists of the coefficient sequences $\psi=\sum_e c_e e$ with $\sum_e|d_e c_e|^2<\infty$. This specifies the joint spectral calculus, not merely formal commutators on test vectors. The total eigenspaces of $\Delta$, including positive ones, may be infinite-dimensional.

For each joint label $(\lambda,a,b)$, let $P_{\lambda,a,b}$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H_{\lambda,a,b}^+\oplus\mathcal H_{\lambda,a,b}^-$. Require reducing-domain commutation with the closed supercharges: $P_{\lambda,a,b}D(T)\subset D(T)$ and $TP_{\lambda,a,b}\psi=P_{\lambda,a,b}T\psi$ for $T=Q,Q^\dagger,\mathsf Q$ and $\psi\in D(T)$. The grading preserves these subspaces and anticommutes with the odd operators on their domains. Thus the given commuting fugacity charges preserve the actual closed supercharge domains and the finite-span joint eigenvector domain; no integrated spectral conclusion is inferred from a common-domain commutator alone.

For positive real fugacities $p,q\in(0,1)$, define $\Xi_{p,q}=p^{J_+}q^{J_-}$ by the supplied joint diagonal calculus, with eigenvalue $p^a q^b$ and its maximal diagonal domain. Define $T_{\beta,p,q}$ first on the finite span of $\mathcal B$ by $T_{\beta,p,q}e=p^a q^b e^{-\beta\lambda}e$. An admissible pair is one for which this positive diagonal operator extends to a bounded trace-class operator for every dimensionless $\beta>0$; denote that extension by $\Xi_{p,q}e^{-\beta\Delta}$. This notation specifies the closed diagonal product, without assuming that an arbitrary product of unbounded operators is everywhere defined. Its supplied-basis diagonal sum is then absolutely convergent. Every joint charge block is finite-dimensional for an admissible pair: its common eigenvalue $p^a q^b e^{-\beta\lambda}$ is strictly positive, so infinitely many orthonormal vectors of that weight would contradict trace-class summability. Infinitely many joint blocks, an infinite protected kernel, and infinite total multiplicity at fixed $\lambda$ are allowed. The **right-handed four-dimensional N=1 superconformal index** is

$$\mathcal I_R(p,q;\beta)=\sum_{e\in\mathcal B^+}\langle\Xi_{p,q}e^{-\beta\Delta}e,e\rangle-\sum_{e\in\mathcal B^-}\langle\Xi_{p,q}e^{-\beta\Delta}e,e\rangle,$$

where $\mathcal B=\mathcal B^+\sqcup\mathcal B^-$ is the supplied joint energy/charge/parity eigenbasis. The positive supercharge gap singles out $\ker\Delta$ as the protected sector, with signed fugacity weight $\Xi_{p,q}$; equality of the full heat supertrace with a trace over that sector is a separate conditional theorem. Other supercharges or central-charge sectors are not silently included. If the weighted trace-class or absolute-convergence condition fails, the expression is only a formal series until a separate regularization and its validity are supplied. No analytic convergence is asserted for all $p,q\in(0,1)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal H=\mathcal H^+\oplus\mathcal H^-$ be a complex Hilbert space with grading operator $\Gamma=+I$ on $\mathcal H^+$ and $\Gamma=-I$ on $\mathcal H^-$. Let $Q$ be a densely defined self-adjoint operator with domain invariant under $\Gamma$ and $Q\Gamma\psi=-\Gamma Q\psi$ for every $\psi\in D(Q)$. Set $H=Q^2$ on the composition domain $D(H)=\{\psi\in D(Q):Q\psi\in D(Q)\}$. For each $\lambda>0$, let $E_\lambda=\{\psi\in D(H):H\psi=\lambda\psi\}$ be finite-dimensional, and put $E_\lambda^\pm=E_\lambda\cap\mathcal H^\pm$. Then $Q$ maps $E_\lambda$ into itself, and

$$U_\lambda:=(Q/\sqrt{\lambda})|_{E_\lambda^+}:E_\lambda^+\longrightarrow E_\lambda^-$$

is a unitary isomorphism, with inverse $(Q/\sqrt{\lambda})|_{E_\lambda^-}$. In particular $\dim E_\lambda^+=\dim E_\lambda^-$. Also $Q\psi=0$ for every zero-energy vector $\psi\in\ker H$. No discrete spectrum or finite-multiplicity assumption is made about energies other than the selected $\lambda$.

derivations.claim: Fix a joint label $(\lambda,a,b)$ with $\lambda>0$. By [F1], its basis vectors lie in the diagonal domain $D(\Delta)=D(\mathsf Q^2)$, and its joint projection reduces $\mathsf Q$. Trace-class summability makes this joint block finite-dimensional: each of its orthonormal basis vectors has the same positive weighted heat diagonal $w=p^a q^b e^{-\beta\lambda}$, so $n$ such vectors would contribute $nw$ for every $n$ if the block were infinite. On this finite reducing block the restriction of $\mathsf Q$ is everywhere defined and symmetric, hence self-adjoint, with square $\lambda I$ and parity anticommutation. Apply [F2] to this restricted Hilbert space: $V_{\lambda,a,b}=\mathsf Q/\sqrt\lambda$ maps its even part unitarily onto its odd part. Their finite dimensions therefore agree.

On the fixed block, $\Xi_{p,q}$ is the scalar $p^a q^b$ and the heat factor is $e^{-\beta\lambda}$. Each supplied even or odd basis vector contributes that same weight. The signed contribution is consequently $p^a q^b e^{-\beta\lambda}(\dim\mathcal H_{\lambda,a,b}^+-\dim\mathcal H_{\lambda,a,b}^-)=0$ by step 1.1. No basis change or cyclic trace of an unbounded product is used.

The full supplied-basis diagonal is absolutely summable by [F1]. For any $\varepsilon>0$, take a finite set of basis vectors with omitted absolute tail below $\varepsilon$. Only finitely many joint blocks meet that set; the sum over those complete blocks differs from the full sum by at most the omitted absolute tail. Thus regrouping by joint charge blocks preserves the sum, even if infinitely many such blocks have the same gap $\lambda$. Every positive-gap block vanishes by step 2.1.

The remaining basis vectors are exactly those with $\lambda=0$. Their heat factor is one and their diagonal weights $p^a q^b$ have finite total absolute sum as a subfamily of the trace-class heat diagonal. Therefore the resulting signed zero-sector trace equals the expression in the Statement and has no $\beta$ dependence, including when the protected kernel is infinite-dimensional.

Statement: If the protected kernel is zero, every index contribution cancels to zero.
Step 1.1: one positive joint (gap,Jplus,Jminus) block is finite by its nonzero constant weight and trace-class summability; the restricted odd self-adjoint charge pairs its parities.
Statement and steps 1.1 and 2.1: whole positive gap eigenspaces may be infinite sums of joint charge blocks; the protected zero sector may likewise be infinite under absolute weighted convergence.
Statement: Beta is positive and fugacities remain inside the declared admissible domain; no beta=0 limit is asserted.
Statement: AC_omega and supplied compatible bases are explicit.

Beta independence of a formal series is not asserted to imply absolute convergence or reducing closed-operator domain identities. Steps 1.1 and 3.1 use those hypotheses independently.

derivations.claim: The matrix of $\mathsf Q$ in $(e_0,e_+,e_-)$ is $\begin{pmatrix}0&0&0\\0&0&\sqrt{E_*}\\0&\sqrt{E_*}&0\end{pmatrix}$, which is self-adjoint. It sends each parity subspace into the other and annihilates $e_0$, so $\Gamma\mathsf Q=-\mathsf Q\Gamma$. Squaring gives $Ke_0=0$ and $Ke_+=E_*e_+$, $Ke_-=E_*e_-$.

Thus the heat operator is diagonal with eigenvalues $1,e^{-\beta E_*},e^{-\beta E_*}$ on $(e_0,e_+,e_-)$; it is finite rank and trace class, and this basis is a complete compatible basis for the pure-point datum under the trace conventions using [A1].

By [F1], $W_E(\beta)=\langle e_0,e_0\rangle+e^{-\beta E_*}\langle e_+,e_+\rangle-e^{-\beta E_*}\langle e_-,e_-\rangle=1+e^{-\beta E_*}-e^{-\beta E_*}=1$. The single even zero mode supplies the net index; the positive-energy even/odd pair cancels for every $\beta>0$.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. A complex Hilbert space is a complete complex inner-product space, with inner product linear in its first variable. A self-adjoint operator $T$ is densely defined and satisfies $D(T)=D(T^*)$ and $T\psi=T^*\psi$ there; nonnegative means $\langle T\psi,\psi\rangle\ge0$ for all $\psi\in D(T)$. A grading operator $\Gamma$ is a bounded self-adjoint involution; its $+1$ and $-1$ eigenspaces are orthogonal, and a densely defined operator $T$ is odd if $D(T)$ is $\Gamma$-invariant and $T\Gamma=-\Gamma T$ there. For operators $A,B$, $D(AB)=\{\psi\in D(B):B\psi\in D(A)\}$ is the composition domain. A Hilbert basis is a complete orthonormal family. Let $S^3=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:|x|=1\}$ have its round metric and standard orientation. The **radial Hilbert space** $\mathcal H_{S^3}$ is the complex Hilbert space supplied by the chosen physical model after quantization on this unit spatial three-sphere; its construction is model input, not proved here. The model record names its gauge group and global form, matter representations, action or other adopted postulates, and the Hilbert-space construction or regulator and measure; the spatial sphere has no boundary, and any other boundary or domain conditions are stated as input. The rotation group is $\operatorname{Spin}(4)=SU(2)_1\times SU(2)_2$. Let $E$ be the dimensionless self-adjoint conformal Hamiltonian, $J_1,J_2$ the self-adjoint Cartan generators of the two rotation factors, and $R$ the self-adjoint $U(1)_R$ charge. Normalize $R$ so that the chosen right-handed Poincare supercharge $Q=\widetilde Q_{\dot -}$ has $R$-charge $+1$ and $J_2$-weight $-\tfrac12$; it has $J_1$-weight zero. Its actual Hilbert adjoint in radial quantization is the conformal supercharge $Q^\dagger=\widetilde S^{\dot -}$. The model supplies a closed densely defined operator $Q$ and its actual Hilbert adjoint $Q^\dagger$, a grading operator $\Gamma$, and a dense linear domain $\mathcal D$ invariant under $\Gamma,Q,Q^\dagger$ and contained in $D(Q^2)\cap D((Q^\dagger)^2)\cap D(QQ^\dagger)\cap D(Q^\dagger Q)$. Require $Q,Q^\dagger$ to be odd, $Q^2=(Q^\dagger)^2=0$ on $\mathcal D$, and the exact positive self-adjoint operator relation

$$\Delta=\frac12\{Q,Q^\dagger\}=E-2J_2-\frac32R\ge0.$$

The protected sector is $\ker\Delta=\ker Q\cap\ker Q^\dagger$, since on the common domain $\langle\Delta\psi,\psi\rangle=\tfrac12(\|Q\psi\|^2+\|Q^\dagger\psi\|^2)$. Define the two dimensionless commuting charges

$$J_+=J_1+J_2+\frac12R,\qquad J_-=J_2-J_1+\frac12R.$$

On a separately supplied dense domain $D(\mathsf Q)\subseteq D(Q)\cap D(Q^\dagger)$, define the odd operator $\mathsf Q=(Q+Q^\dagger)/\sqrt2$ and require it to be self-adjoint and to satisfy $\mathsf Q^2=\Delta$ as a closed-operator equality. Its domain is $\Gamma$-invariant and $\Gamma\mathsf Q=-\mathsf Q\Gamma$ there. Supply a simultaneous pure-point decomposition for $\Delta,J_+,J_-$ and $\Gamma$, with a compatible complete orthonormal basis $\mathcal B=\mathcal B^+\sqcup\mathcal B^-$. More explicitly, the basis vectors have real charge eigenvalues $(\lambda,a,b)$, with $\lambda\ge0$, and span the joint subspaces $\mathcal H_{\lambda,a,b}^\pm$; the distinct joint labels form a supplied countable set. Each closed self-adjoint charge has its maximal diagonal domain: for eigenvalues $d_e$ its domain consists of the coefficient sequences $\psi=\sum_e c_e e$ with $\sum_e|d_e c_e|^2<\infty$. This specifies the joint spectral calculus, not merely formal commutators on test vectors. The total eigenspaces of $\Delta$, including positive ones, may be infinite-dimensional.

For each joint label $(\lambda,a,b)$, let $P_{\lambda,a,b}$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H_{\lambda,a,b}^+\oplus\mathcal H_{\lambda,a,b}^-$. Require reducing-domain commutation with the closed supercharges: $P_{\lambda,a,b}D(T)\subset D(T)$ and $TP_{\lambda,a,b}\psi=P_{\lambda,a,b}T\psi$ for $T=Q,Q^\dagger,\mathsf Q$ and $\psi\in D(T)$. The grading preserves these subspaces and anticommutes with the odd operators on their domains. Thus the given commuting fugacity charges preserve the actual closed supercharge domains and the finite-span joint eigenvector domain; no integrated spectral conclusion is inferred from a common-domain commutator alone.

For positive real fugacities $p,q\in(0,1)$, define $\Xi_{p,q}=p^{J_+}q^{J_-}$ by the supplied joint diagonal calculus, with eigenvalue $p^a q^b$ and its maximal diagonal domain. Define $T_{\beta,p,q}$ first on the finite span of $\mathcal B$ by $T_{\beta,p,q}e=p^a q^b e^{-\beta\lambda}e$. An admissible pair is one for which this positive diagonal operator extends to a bounded trace-class operator for every dimensionless $\beta>0$; denote that extension by $\Xi_{p,q}e^{-\beta\Delta}$. This notation specifies the closed diagonal product, without assuming that an arbitrary product of unbounded operators is everywhere defined. Its supplied-basis diagonal sum is then absolutely convergent. Every joint charge block is finite-dimensional for an admissible pair: its common eigenvalue $p^a q^b e^{-\beta\lambda}$ is strictly positive, so infinitely many orthonormal vectors of that weight would contradict trace-class summability. Infinitely many joint blocks, an infinite protected kernel, and infinite total multiplicity at fixed $\lambda$ are allowed. The **right-handed four-dimensional N=1 superconformal index** is

$$\mathcal I_R(p,q;\beta)=\sum_{e\in\mathcal B^+}\langle\Xi_{p,q}e^{-\beta\Delta}e,e\rangle-\sum_{e\in\mathcal B^-}\langle\Xi_{p,q}e^{-\beta\Delta}e,e\rangle,$$

where $\mathcal B=\mathcal B^+\sqcup\mathcal B^-$ is the supplied joint energy/charge/parity eigenbasis. The positive supercharge gap singles out $\ker\Delta$ as the protected sector, with signed fugacity weight $\Xi_{p,q}$; equality of the full heat supertrace with a trace over that sector is a separate conditional theorem. Other supercharges or central-charge sectors are not silently included. If the weighted trace-class or absolute-convergence condition fails, the expression is only a formal series until a separate regularization and its validity are supplied. No analytic convergence is asserted for all $p,q\in(0,1)$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and take the exact right-handed four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal operator data on the unit round $S^3$ specified in the earlier definition. In particular, $\mathsf Q=(Q+Q^\dagger)/\sqrt2$ is self-adjoint and odd, $\Delta=\mathsf Q^2\ge0$, and the model supplies the simultaneous pure-point energy/charge/parity basis and reducing-domain projection identities in that definition. Neither the protected kernel nor a total positive-gap eigenspace is required to be finite-dimensional. For an admissible $0<p,q<1$, $\Xi_{p,q}=p^{J_+}q^{J_-}$ has eigenvalue $p^a q^b$ on each joint block $\mathcal H_{\lambda,a,b}$, and the diagonal products $T_{\beta,p,q}=\Xi_{p,q}e^{-\beta\Delta}$ extend to bounded trace-class operators for all $\beta>0$. Then

$$\mathcal I_R(p,q;\beta)=\sum_{e\in E_0^+}\langle\Xi_{p,q}e,e\rangle-\sum_{e\in E_0^-}\langle\Xi_{p,q}e,e\rangle$$

for all $\beta>0$, where $E_0^\pm$ are supplied compatible orthonormal bases of $\ker\Delta\cap\mathcal H^\pm$. The zero-sector sums converge absolutely even when the protected kernel is infinite-dimensional, and the superconformal index is independent of $\beta$. No assertion is made for continuous spectrum, a nonconvergent formal trace, or an unproved regularization.

derivations.claim: For the scalar letter, $\Delta=E-2J_2-\tfrac32R=1-0-1=0$ and $J_+=J_-=1/3$, so its signed fugacity weight is $(pq)^{1/3}$.

For $\bar\psi_{\dot +}$, $\Delta=\tfrac32-1-\tfrac12=0$ and $J_+=J_-=\tfrac12+\tfrac16=2/3$; its fermion parity contributes the negative weight $-(pq)^{2/3}$. Each $D_p$ adds one to $J_+$ and zero to $J_-$, while each $D_q$ adds zero to $J_+$ and one to $J_-$, and both preserve $\Delta=0$.

Summing the scalar and fermion towers gives $i_\chi(p,q)=\sum_{m,n\ge0}((pq)^{1/3}-(pq)^{2/3})p^mq^n$. Since $0<p,q<1$, the geometric sums are $\sum_{m,n\ge0}p^mq^n=((1-p)(1-q))^{-1}$, yielding the displayed single-letter formula.

For a bosonic letter of weight $x$, all occupations contribute $1+x+x^2+\cdots=(1-x)^{-1}$; for a fermionic letter, the two allowed occupations contribute $1-x$. Applying these factors to each derivative mode produces the rectangular partial product in the Example. For finite mode sets this is an ordinary product of occupation sums; passage to the infinite product requires absolute convergence.

Put $a=(pq)^{1/3}<1$, $b=(pq)^{2/3}<1$, $x_{mn}=ap^mq^n$, and $y_{mn}=bp^mq^n$. Their sums are $a/((1-p)(1-q))$ and $b/((1-p)(1-q))$. For a finite rectangular mode set $S$, the sum of absolute occupation weights supported in $S$ is $P_S=\prod_{(m,n)\in S}(1+y_{mn})/(1-x_{mn})$. Since $-\log(1-x)\le x/(1-a)$ for $0\le x\le a$ and $\log(1+y)\le y$ for $y\ge0$, one has $P_S\le\exp((a/(1-a)+b)/((1-p)(1-q)))$. Every finite family of finite-support occupation states is supported in some such $S$, so its absolute weight sum is bounded by this same finite constant. Thus the entire occupation-weight family is absolutely summable. Increasing rectangles exhaust all its states, justifying the signed trace/product identity from step 3.1. Moreover, $|(1-y_{mn})/(1-x_{mn})-1|\le(x_{mn}+y_{mn})/(1-a)$, so the displayed product is absolutely convergent.

On the protected occupation basis let $\Xi_0$ have the positive diagonal weights just summed. It is bounded, and its finite-rank diagonal truncations have operator-norm error at most the omitted weight sum, which tends to zero. Hence it is compact, with summable singular values given by these nonnegative diagonal weights, and therefore trace class. The heat factor is one on this sector for every $\beta>0$. Its orthogonal direct sum with the complementary weighted heat operator supplied by [A2] is bounded trace class: the two diagonal weight families are summable, and finite-rank truncations again converge in operator norm. This proves full admissibility in [F1], using [A2]'s independent complementary-sector assumptions. Now [F2] applies and identifies the protected trace with the full superconformal heat supertrace, independent of $\beta$.

The finite-support occupation basis includes the even vacuum and exhausts the protected sector by explicit hypothesis; no gauge constraints or extra relations are inferred. Bounds -log(1-x)<=x/(1-a) and log(1+y)<=y show absolute occupation sum finite; increasing rectangles exhaust every finite-support state and justify product/trace equality. All 0<p,q<1, including near endpoints, are covered but endpoints excluded.
